metadata.description: Primary-source catalog for LLM/agent evaluation and optimization methodology: LLM-as-judge reliability/bias and advanced judging (juries, fine-tuned judges, calibration), eval frameworks, threshold calibration, eval statistics, fine-tuning decision loops (SFT, RFT, graders, PEFT/LoRA/QLoRA, preference tuning), test-time compute, data construction, distillation, online/production eval, safety/red-team eval, and reproducibility/contamination. Verify framework and fine-tuning APIs against official docs before recommending a specific call.
metadata.title: AI Evals - Sources

judge_reliability_research.name: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
judge_reliability_research.relevance: Canonical LLM-as-judge paper. Documents position bias, verbosity bias, and self-enhancement (self-preference) bias, and validates judge-human agreement. Foundational for the bias taxonomy.

judge_reliability_research.name: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
judge_reliability_research.relevance: Quantifies position bias in pairwise LLM judging and proposes balanced-position calibration (run both orderings). Basis for the both-orderings-must-agree control.

judge_reliability_research.name: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
judge_reliability_research.relevance: Rubric/chain-of-thought judge design with form-filling, plus probability-weighted scoring (expectation over score-token logprobs). Basis for the CoT-before-verdict and probability-weighted scoring guidance in advanced-judging.md.

judge_reliability_research.name: Length-Controlled AlpacaEval: A Simple Way to Debias Automatic Evaluators
judge_reliability_research.relevance: 2024. Quantifies and corrects length/verbosity bias in LLM-judge leaderboards via regression-based length control. Basis for treating length bias as a measurable, correctable confound rather than just a prompt instruction.

judge_reliability_research.name: Judging the Judges: Evaluating Alignment and Vulnerabilities in LLMs-as-Judges (Bavaresco et al.)
judge_reliability_research.relevance: 2024 survey/benchmark of LLM-judge reliability across tasks; documents where judges agree with humans and where they fail. Basis for 'measure judge-human agreement, do not assume it' across threshold-derivation.md and advanced-judging.md.

advanced_judging_research.name: Replacing Judges with Juries (PoLL: Panel of LLm evaluators)
advanced_judging_research.relevance: 2024. Shows a panel of smaller diverse judges agrees with humans better and cheaper than one large judge, and reduces intra-model self-preference bias. Basis for the juries/ensembles section in advanced-judging.md.

advanced_judging_research.name: Prometheus 2: An Open Source LM Specialized in Evaluating Other LMs
advanced_judging_research.relevance: 2024. Open fine-tuned judge model supporting direct-assessment and pairwise grading against custom rubrics. Reference for the prompted-vs-fine-tuned judge tradeoff; verify current model/license before adopting.

advanced_judging_research.name: JudgeLM: Fine-tuned Large Language Models are Scalable Judges
advanced_judging_research.relevance: Fine-tuned judge with bias-mitigation training (swap/reference augmentation). Supporting reference for fine-tuned-judge viability and bias controls in advanced-judging.md.

eval_statistics_methods.name: scipy.stats.bootstrap
eval_statistics_methods.relevance: Reference implementation for bootstrap confidence intervals (BCa and percentile) used throughout eval-statistics.md. Verify current API/params per scipy version.

eval_statistics_methods.name: statsmodels: McNemar's test (contingency tables)
eval_statistics_methods.relevance: Reference implementation of McNemar's paired test for binary same-case comparisons (the correct test for 'A passed cases B failed'). Used in eval-statistics.md.

eval_statistics_methods.name: Benjamini & Hochberg, Controlling the False Discovery Rate
eval_statistics_methods.relevance: Foundational FDR multiple-comparison correction; default for slice/metric dashboards in eval-statistics.md. statsmodels provides multipletests(method='fdr_bh').

eval_statistics_methods.name: CUPED: Improving the Sensitivity of Online Controlled Experiments (Deng et al.)
eval_statistics_methods.relevance: Variance-reduction via pre-experiment covariate adjustment; basis for the CUPED-style variance reduction note in eval-statistics.md (offline paired and online A/B).

safety_and_redteam_research.name: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models (GCG)
safety_and_redteam_research.relevance: Automated adversarial suffix attacks; basis for testing adaptive/automated jailbreaks (not just static suites) in safety-redteam-eval.md.

safety_and_redteam_research.name: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
safety_and_redteam_research.relevance: Defines indirect prompt injection via retrieved/tool content — the dominant agentic attack. Basis for the planted-instruction injection methodology in safety-redteam-eval.md.

safety_and_redteam_research.name: XSTest: A Test Suite for Identifying Exaggerated Safety Behaviours
safety_and_redteam_research.relevance: Benign-but-adjacent prompts to measure over-refusal. Basis for scoring the 'should-comply' set alongside the harmful set in safety-redteam-eval.md.

safety_and_redteam_research.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
safety_and_redteam_research.relevance: Practitioner taxonomy of LLM risks (prompt injection, excessive agency, data exfiltration). Maps to the agentic-safety eval categories in safety-redteam-eval.md. Verify current version.

frameworks.name: Inspect AI (UK AISI)
frameworks.relevance: Solver/scorer eval framework for agentic and tool-use tasks; supports model graders. Verify current scorer API before copying snippets.

frameworks.name: lighteval (Hugging Face)
frameworks.relevance: Multi-backend benchmark runner. v0.13 uses one-file-one-task; verify task-string format and backend flags per version.

frameworks.name: lm-evaluation-harness (EleutherAI)
frameworks.relevance: Reproducible academic benchmark harness; contamination-aware. The benchmark lingua franca for open models.

frameworks.name: Ragas
frameworks.relevance: RAG faithfulness/context metrics and synthetic testset generation. Read what each metric computes before gating; verify metric defs per version.

frameworks.name: DeepEval
frameworks.relevance: pytest-style LLM eval assertions (G-Eval and others) for CI regression gating in app repos.

frameworks.name: promptfoo
frameworks.relevance: Config-driven prompt/app matrix testing with assertions and model graders; fast for prompt A/B in CI. Acquired by OpenAI March 9, 2026 — remains open source; roadmap now OpenAI-aligned.

frameworks.name: Promptfoo Joining OpenAI
frameworks.relevance: Acquisition announcement (March 9, 2026): OpenAI acquires Promptfoo; product remains open source; roadmap aligns with OpenAI infrastructure. Factor into vendor-neutrality decisions for multi-provider eval stacks.

frameworks.name: Braintrust Docs
frameworks.relevance: Hosted experiment/dataset/score tracking platform; a logging and iteration layer, not a metric source by itself.

frameworks.name: Langfuse Documentation
frameworks.relevance: Open-source, self-hostable LLM observability and online eval sampling platform. OTel-native tracing with online eval scoring hooks. Use for production-trace sampling and self-hosted deployments. Verify current SDK and eval sampling API before use.

frameworks.name: Arize Phoenix Documentation
frameworks.relevance: Open-source, vendor-agnostic LLM observability and RAG eval framework with OTel-native tracing and enterprise production monitoring. Use for retrieval attribution in production and multi-provider eval stacks.

frameworks.name: W&B Weave Documentation
frameworks.relevance: Weights & Biases tracing and eval layer for ML teams already using W&B for training runs. Covers experiment tracking, production tracing, and custom graders. Best fit when the team is W&B-native.

frameworks.name: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation
frameworks.relevance: Managed model-comparison and RAG evaluation (Knowledge Bases) on Bedrock. Supports LLM-as-judge, human, and automatic metrics. Native option for AWS/Bedrock-stack teams; verify current job types, eligible models, and metric support before use.

benchmarks_and_contamination.name: HELM (Holistic Evaluation of Language Models)
benchmarks_and_contamination.relevance: Multi-metric, multi-scenario benchmark methodology; reference for slice-aware, multi-dimension evaluation rather than single-number gates.

benchmarks_and_contamination.name: OpenAI Evals
benchmarks_and_contamination.relevance: Registry-based eval framework and template patterns (match, model-graded). Useful as a structural reference for eval/grader templates.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: OpenAI Model Optimization Guide
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: Official model-optimization overview tying evals, prompt optimization, and fine-tuning together. Use to verify current OpenAI platform flow before recommending an optimization path.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: OpenAI Supervised Fine-Tuning Guide
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: Official SFT workflow and dataset guidance. Basis for eval-first SFT gating and current JSONL/job requirements; verify eligible models and schemas.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: OpenAI Fine-Tuning Best Practices
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: Official iteration guidance on data quality, diversity, and diagnosing weak fine-tune results. Supports the training-data-quality-over-volume guidance.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: OpenAI Reinforcement Fine-Tuning Guide
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: Official RFT workflow using programmable graders for reasoning-domain optimization. Verify current model eligibility, grader schema, and dataset requirements.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: OpenAI Graders Guide
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: Official grader types used for evals and fine-tuning. Supports guidance on deterministic, model, code, and multi-grader reward composition.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: OpenAI Model Selection Guide
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: Official guidance that fine-tuning should follow baseline/model-selection work, not replace it. Verify current model tradeoffs and availability.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: Hugging Face TRL Documentation
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: Official transformers reinforcement-learning and preference-training library docs (SFTTrainer, DPOTrainer, related trainers). Verify current trainer APIs.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: Hugging Face PEFT LoRA Guide
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: Official PEFT LoRA guide for parameter-efficient adaptation. Verify current target-module, adapter, quantization, and merge/deploy APIs.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: Axolotl Documentation
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: Open-source fine-tuning framework documentation for SFT, LoRA/QLoRA, preference, and reward-model workflows. Verify current config keys before use.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: Unsloth Documentation
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: Open-source efficient fine-tuning docs for LoRA/QLoRA workflows. Useful for local/open-model adaptation planning; verify current notebooks and hardware support.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: Amazon Bedrock Custom Model Import
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: AWS path for bringing a fine-tuned open model into Bedrock's serving layer. Use instead of HF/OpenAI fine-tuning paths when the stack is AWS-native. Verify current supported model architectures and import requirements.

fine_tuning_platform_docs.name: Amazon SageMaker Training Jobs
fine_tuning_platform_docs.relevance: Primary AWS fine-tuning surface for SFT and RL-style training on managed infrastructure. Replaces HF/OpenAI fine-tuning paths for AWS-stack users. Verify current container images, instance types, and SageMaker Clarify integration for training transparency.

fine_tuning_research_methods.name: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
fine_tuning_research_methods.relevance: InstructGPT/RLHF paper. Foundational reference for SFT plus preference/reward optimization and human-evaluation comparison against base models.

fine_tuning_research_methods.name: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
fine_tuning_research_methods.relevance: Canonical DPO paper. Basis for choosing preference tuning when pairwise preference labels are available and reward-model/RL complexity is unnecessary.

fine_tuning_research_methods.name: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
fine_tuning_research_methods.relevance: Canonical parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that freezes base weights and trains low-rank adapter matrices. Basis for PEFT/adapter method selection.

fine_tuning_research_methods.name: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
fine_tuning_research_methods.relevance: Canonical quantized LoRA method. Basis for low-memory open-model adaptation guidance and for treating QLoRA as a compute method, not a product-quality guarantee.

optimization_method_research.name: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
optimization_method_research.relevance: Foundational prompting-pattern source for decomposed reasoning. Use as background for reasoning-slice prompt baselines before heavier optimization.

optimization_method_research.name: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
optimization_method_research.relevance: Canonical sample-and-aggregate test-time compute method. Basis for pass@k, majority-vote, and marginal-cost gates in llm-optimization-technique-map.md.

optimization_method_research.name: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
optimization_method_research.relevance: Search-over-thoughts inference method. Useful for high-value planning/reasoning slices where verifier or heuristic quality can be evaluated.

optimization_method_research.name: A Survey of Test-Time Compute: From Intuitive Inference to Deliberate Reasoning
optimization_method_research.relevance: Recent taxonomy for inference-time scaling methods. Use for source refresh before recommending newer test-time compute variants.

optimization_method_research.name: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
optimization_method_research.relevance: Critique/retry and verbal feedback loop for agents. Basis for retry-lift and trace-grounded feedback gates.

optimization_method_research.name: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
optimization_method_research.relevance: Self-feedback refinement method. Useful as a low-lift inference-time baseline before fine-tuning; requires self-feedback reliability checks.

optimization_method_research.name: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
optimization_method_research.relevance: Synthetic instruction generation and filtering recipe. Basis for data-construction guidance with human anchors and leakage controls.

optimization_method_research.name: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment
optimization_method_research.relevance: High-quality-small-data alignment reference. Basis for 'curation before volume' and lift-per-example gates.

optimization_method_research.name: WizardCoder: Empowering Code Large Language Models with Evol-Instruct
optimization_method_research.relevance: Domain-specific Evol-Instruct application for code. Supports synthetic hard-example generation guidance with domain-specific validation.

optimization_method_research.name: RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG
optimization_method_research.relevance: Retrieval-augmented fine-tuning recipe with distractors. Basis for grounded-answer, citation-support, and distractor-robustness gates.

optimization_method_research.name: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
optimization_method_research.relevance: Preference-alignment loss for desirable/undesirable binary feedback. Basis for choosing KTO when pairwise labels are unavailable.

optimization_method_research.name: ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model
optimization_method_research.relevance: Single-stage SFT plus preference penalty without a reference model. Basis for reference-free preference tuning tradeoffs.

optimization_method_research.name: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
optimization_method_research.relevance: Reference-free DPO-style preference optimization with length-aware reward formulation. Basis for memory/cost-sensitive preference tuning guidance.

optimization_method_research.name: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
optimization_method_research.relevance: Introduces GRPO-style verifiable-reward optimization in an open reasoning setting. Basis for RLVR/GRPO verifier-first gates.

optimization_method_research.name: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
optimization_method_research.relevance: Reasoning RL technical report. Supports the guidance that verifiable rewards can move reasoning when verifier quality is high.

optimization_method_research.name: Distilling Step-by-Step! Outperforming Larger Language Models with Less Training Data and Smaller Model Sizes
optimization_method_research.relevance: Rationale-augmented distillation method. Basis for student-vs-teacher quality/cost Pareto gates.

optimization_method_research.name: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
optimization_method_research.relevance: RLAIF and critique/revision source. Basis for principle-guided data construction, reward-model cautions, and safety replay.

optimization_method_research.name: Self-Rewarding Language Models
optimization_method_research.relevance: Self-generated reward/judge training method. Useful as a high-risk validate-only idea because self-judging can amplify judge bias.

optimization_method_research.name: MDP-GRPO: Stabilized Group Relative Policy Optimization for Multi-Constraint Instruction Following
optimization_method_research.relevance: Emerging GRPO stabilization direction surfaced in arXiv scan. Track as validate-only until implementation support and independent reproduction are clear.
